newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firms up at close on U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firms up at close on U.S. long bond.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed firmer across the board on Thursday as yields on U.S. long bonds receded and month-end demand for dollars subsided, traders said.
"The month closes tomorrow, and dealers usually cover (dollar) positions in advance, so we hardly saw anyone buy dollars today," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.9 and 1.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8330/7.8360 and 7.8220/7.8270 per dollar.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds fell to 6.88 percent from 6.90 percent on Wednesday.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.9 of a centavo firmer at 7.8230/7.8270 per dollar.
"The bourse is doing well and U.S. bonds are strong," another trader said. "It all helps to consolidate the peso at current levels."
The leading share IPC index was up 0.99 percent at 3,667.57 points when the foreign exchange market closed in Mexico.
